item.title: Policy Officer
item.description: Do you want to work at the heart of heritage, and help to champion its future? The Heritage Alliance is seeking a part-time Policy Officer to join our small advocacy team at an exciting time for the sector. The role will support with all elements of our research, policy development and political engagement. This role would be ideally suited to someone looking to gain experience in the heritage sector who has a keen interest in the UK policy and political landscape. The Heritage Alliance is the national umbrella body for heritage, a charity with over 200 organisational members. This is an exciting and wide-ranging role, requiring a dynamic, proactive and reliable individual. The role presents an ideal opportunity for someone looking to develop skills in policy research and development, political communications, and parliamentary monitoring. The role gives an opportunity to work with a small team to build expertise in a diverse range of policy areas including planning, historic landscapes, education and skills, and funding. Key priorities for 2027 include advocating for heritage through the government’s devolution and rewiring the state agenda, publishing and promoting reports on placemaking and academic partnerships, and strengthening our relationships with the new administration and regional decision-makers. Applicants should be persuasive writers and communicators, have a passion for advocacy and policy, strong analytical skills, and the ability to deliver at pace. Whilst a demonstrable interest in heritage is important, direct experience is not essential. Key Responsibilities: Researching across a wide range of policy briefs affecting the Alliance’s members; Drafting letters, briefings and consultation responses for government and parliament as needed; Co-ordinating, minuting and actioning the work of the Alliance’s Advocacy and Working Groups in liaison with their Chairs; Monitoring parliamentary activity for heritage-related developments in both houses and in select committees; Supporting with the development and drafting of policy and insight reports, advocacy resources and publications; Occasional support of the Heritage Alliance’s communications and events products, including producing copy and reporting on government news and policy developments for our newsletters. To Apply Please click the Apply button below to find out more about this role and to download the Application Form. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. The closing date for applications is 9 November with interviews held at our offices shortly afterwards. The starting date for the new role would ideally be December 2026 or early January 2027. This role is part-time (0.5 FTE) for an initial 1-year contract with potential to extend. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Monday 9th November 2026

item.title: Senior Account Manager (Energy Media Relations)
item.description: Join the PubAffairs Network Established in January 2002, PubAffairs is the premier network and leading resource for the public affairs, government relations, policy and communications industry. The PubAffairs network numbers over 4,000 members and is free to join. PubAffairs operates a general e-Newsletter, as well as a number of other specific group e-Newsletters which are also available to join by completing our registration form. The PubAffairs e-Newsletters are used to keep members informed about upcoming PubAffairs events and networking opportunities, job vacancies, public affairs news, training courses, stakeholder events, publications, discount offers and other pieces of useful information related to the public affairs and communications industry. Join the Network

item.title: Researcher (Internship)
item.description: JBP Communications is a national consultancy at the heart of Westminster. From our office opposite Parliament, we help organisations navigate politics, shape debate and make their voices heard. The role Start your career where politics, places and people meet. Working from JBP’s Westminster office, you will support public affairs and strategic communications campaigns, helping clients understand the political landscape, engage decisionmakers and communicate with impact. This opportunity is open to recent graduates, college leavers and career starters who are curious, politically engaged and ready to learn. While previous experience is not required, a strong knowledge of current affairs and politics is essential. What we’re looking for You will be politically engaged, interested in local government and confident working at pace under pressure. Strong research and writing skills are necessary; knowledge of devolution, planning or regional growth is a bonus. You will be expected to bring attention to detail, good organisational skills and the ability to turn complex information into clear, concise summaries. We’re looking for someone who asks questions, takes initiative and enjoys working as part of a team. From tracking the day’s political story and researching MPs and councillors to supporting consultations, events and client communications, you will contribute from day one. Key responsibilities Monitor political, policy and media developments. Research MPs, councillors, journalists and community stakeholders. Draft briefings, consultation materials and digital content. Support client campaigns, events and political engagement. Produce and maintain stakeholder lists and help coordinate meeting and event invitations. Take accurate meeting notes and track follow-up actions for the team. Contract: Three months, with an opportunity for extension or permanent placement. To Apply Please click on the Apply button below to submit your CV of up to two pages and a one-page covering letter. When applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Interviews w/c 16 November. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Wednesday 11th November 2026

item.title: Policy and Public Affairs Manager
item.description: The Chartered Institute of Ecology and Environmental Management (CIEEM) is the professional membership body for ecologists and environmental managers working to protect and enhance the natural environment. We are recognised by our members and external stakeholders as the voice of the profession through our effective, evidence-based input into, and support for, policy and practice. We are delighted to offer an exciting opportunity for a Policy and Public Affairs Manager to significantly contribute to our work influencing governments, parliaments and the media across the UK nations and Ireland. Reporting to the Head of Policy, you will be part of our Management Team. About the role The successful candidate will: a. Play a pivotal role in CIEEM’s public affairs work, helping to make sure our members’ voices are heard where decisions are made. b. Build and maintain relationships with parliamentarians, civil servants, journalists, peer organisations and networks. c. Manage our media relations on policy issues, from rapid responses to comment requests to proactive stories, op-eds, social media activity and campaigns. d. Help turn the evidence and expertise of our members into clear, credible positions for political and public audiences, in each UK nation and Ireland. e. Manage key staff to help deliver our policy work. Why this role? These are both exciting and challenging times for the ecology and environment sector. Environmental policy is diverging across the UK nations and Ireland, with significant change under way in, for example, approaches to nature recovery and government priorities. This is a unique opportunity to help shape the political and public debate for the benefit of nature and society. You will deliver real impact using creativity, sound prioritisation and the expertise of our members and volunteers. You will join a small but dynamic and dedicated team where your ideas, energy and judgement can make a real difference. About you We are looking for someone who is: a. An experienced public affairs or policy professional with a track record of securing political or media outcomes. b. Politically astute, with an understanding of how politics differs across the UK nations and Ireland, and of how to protect our non-party-political credibility. c. An excellent communicator, able to translate science and evidence for political and public audiences and to build credible relationships with parliamentarians, civil servants and journalists. d. Ideally, an experienced manager of people and projects with the judgement to prioritise in a small team. Experience of the ecology and nature conservation sector or the professional body sector is welcome but not essential. Preference will be given to candidates with strong public affairs experience. Benefits As part of our commitment to making CIEEM a great place to work, we offer a comprehensive reward and benefits package which includes: flexible working arrangements; 25 days leave plus public holidays; a generous Workplace Qualifying Pension Scheme with CIEEM contributing up to 10% of gross salary (dependent on employee’s contribution) for eligible employees; professional development opportunities; and access to an employee assistance programme. For more information please see our ‘Working for CIEEM’ webpage . Location This post will be based at the CIEEM office in Ampfield (near Romsey in Hampshire) with the option of a hybrid arrangement with up to 50% of the time working from home. Alternatively, for those living more than an hour’s travel from Ampfield, the role can be home-based with occasional travel to the office. Regardless of location, some travel to Westminster and other key locations across the UK and Ireland will be required. We will also consider other flexible working arrangements. Salary: £42,410 - £45,643 per annum (dependent on experience). When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Closing Date: 12 noon Wednesday 25 November 2026. Interview Dates: Friday 11 and Tuesday 15 December 2026. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion CIEEM is committed to promoting a culture of inclusion, fairness, and belonging amongst its employees. We welcome applications from all, irrespective of background and are committed to making reasonable adjustments for candidates and employees. For further information, please see our ED&I Mission Statement . Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 12:00pm on Wednesday 25th November 2026
